quiz_title: 🤖 PicToBlox Challenge 6: Clone Armies & Smart Game Decisions

questions.question: What happens when you execute the 'create clone of (myself)' control block during gameplay?
options: It spawns an exact, independent copy of the sprite that runs its own clone scripts
It draws a green circle on the background track
questions.explanation: Spot on! Cloning spawns active copies of our sprites on the fly, allowing us to generate multiple flying ducks, falling basketballs, or obstacle pipes easily.

questions.question: Why is it important to use the 'delete this clone' control block when a clone completes its action (like hitting a wall)?
options: To clear memory and prevent the game from reaching its maximum clone limits, which would freeze the program
To make the sprite change colors
To play a winning chime sound
To speed up the player's paddle
questions.explanation: Correct! Deleting finished clones frees up system resources, keeping the game smooth and within the active clone limit of 300.

questions.question: When combining blocks using the logical 'or' operator, when does the entire check return True?
options: Both conditions must be completely True
At least one of the conditions (left or right) must be True
Both conditions must be completely False
questions.explanation: Excellent! The 'or' operator is flexible. It evaluates as True if either the left side, the right side, or both sides are True.

questions.question: How does the 'if () then {} else {}' control block differ from a simple 'if () then' block?
options: It can only hold sound blocks
It makes a two-way decision: executing the top script if the condition is True, and the bottom 'else' script if the condition is False
It does not differ at all
questions.explanation: Great! The 'if-else' block provides two separate pathways, guaranteeing that one of the two code blocks will execute depending on the check.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to spawn (create) a clone of 'myself' when the 'space' key is pressed.
questions.task_hint: Write: when space key pressed -> create clone of myself
questions.explanation: Perfect! Attaching clone-creation to event blocks lets players fire projectiles or spawn items interactively.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Write an 'if else' block script checking if the mouse is down. If it is, say 'Hit!'; otherwise, say 'Miss!'
questions.task_hint: Write: if mouse down? then say Hit! else say Miss!
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Using two-way if-else statements provides a highly interactive and feedback-rich experience for your players.
